newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex outlines Cactus natgas plant blast costs.
newsitem.headline: Pemex outlines Cactus natgas plant blast costs.

text.p: The director of the gas unit of Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos told Mexican deputies Wednesday the total cost of damage from the explosion at Cactus gas plant will be $199.5 million by the end of the year.

Pemex Gas director Marcos Ramirez added additional costs of $56 million have been incurred in lost production from the July 26 blast at Mexico's largest gas complex, which killed at least six workers.
The blast slashed natural gas production capacity and temporarily halted production in the complex in Chiapas state.
Two units at Cactus, which had a total capacity of 1.6 billion cubic feet per day (cfd), were almost completely destroyed. Each unit produced 500 million cfd.
Pemex director general Adrian Lajous, speaking at a presentation of Cactus findings to the Chamber of Deputies' Energy Commission, reiterated that human error was to blame for the blast.
Lajous said the blast stemmed from a gas leakage after a valve was left open.
